messages:
maria: Proposal — add an automatic pause guard for gradual rollouts that combines latency SLO, error rate, and a per-request token-cost delta. Thinking of a single composite gate that can be tuned per-customer. Thoughts?

sunil: +1 on composite but we should keep signals independent for visibility. users will want to know which signal tripped (latency vs cost vs error).

danny: fwiw we already emit per-route latency histograms and token_count per response. The missing piece is a simple evaluator that can run in the rollout controller.

maria: yes. UX idea: a compact three-pill status (latency / errors / cost) in Console rollouts. Each pill shows baseline vs canary delta and a reason when it pauses.

oliver: what about oscillation? small transient blips could pause a rollout unnecessarily. need hysteresis and minimal sample window. i'd prefer a policy that requires 2/3 signals or sustained violation for N minutes.

kevin: Agree. Suggest default: require either (a) sustained violation for 3 minutes, or (b) any violation that exceeds absolute thresholds (e.g., p95 latency +200ms) OR cost increase >20% AND error rate >0.5%. Those are just defaults we can expose.

maria: sounds reasonable. Also want an API shape for rollout configs: e.g.
```
{ "phases": [ {"pct": 5, "duration": "10m"}, {"pct": 25, "duration": "20m"} ],
  "guards": {"latency": {"p95_delta_ms": 200, "sustained_minutes":3},
             "errors": {"error_rate_pct": 0.5},
             "cost": {"pct_increase": 20}}
}
```
Is that too prescriptive?

sunil: good start. we should support both absolute and relative baselines. Some customers want absolute SLOs (p95 < 250ms) instead of deltas. Also add "action": ["pause","rollback","notify"] per guard.

danny: telemetry question: when a rollout pauses we must capture the full sample: request id, model version, prompt length distribution, and cache hit ratio. otherwise hard to debug cost spikes. That data volume is big — maybe sample at 1% but keep a trigger-mode full dump on pause.

oliver: +1 on trigger-mode dump. Also add a synthetic traffic runner option to reproduce the issue against the canary model in a sandbox. Could be a separate job in Console.

kevin: operational concern: auto-pause should not impact high-priority enterprise customers without explicit opt-in. default behavior: auto-pause enabled for orgs < enterprise-tier; for enterprise require admins to enable or have canary ownership.

maria: good catch. add: rollout "guard_mode": ["opt-in","opt-out","enforced"] per org. default opt-in for hosted.

deploy-bot: deploy event: canary rollout started for model v2.3 -> 5% traffic (maria).

danny: one more edge: token-cost regressions can be from prompts changing (longer prompts) not model. we should match prompt-length histograms pre/post and if prompt shift explains cost, don’t pause model. add a prompt-drift detector that compares median prompt tokens.

sunil: yep, include prompt tokens and user segment breakdown (routes/accounts) so we can see if a single tenant caused the delta.

maria: action items: (1) draft API schema for guards + guard_mode + actions (2) implement evaluator with hysteresis + trigger-mode dump (3) Console UI: three-pill status + reason + quick-replay button (4) enterprise opt-in defaults. I'll spin PR for (1).

oliver: if you want i can put together a quick mock for the Console pill and the replay flow.

maria: please do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
